elements.quote: Following PRISMA guidelines, a comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane databases from inception to 1 May 2025.

elements.quote: Eight studies comprising 3024 patients were included.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the total number of studies and participants, but does not summarize relevant study characteristics (e.g., study design, location).

elements.quote: ESD was associated with significantly lower local recurrence compared to EMR (0.62% versus 12.02%; OR 0.07, 95% CI 0.03-0.13, p < 0.01). However, ESD had a higher risk of perforation (5.38% versus 1.53%; OR 3.16, 95% CI 1.89-5.29, p < 0.01). No significant difference was found in delayed bleeding rates (3.65% versus 3.75%; OR 1.01, 95% CI 0.65-1.55, p = 0.98).
elements.reason: The abstract presents results for the main outcomes with numbers of studies and participants implied by the context.

elements.quote: ESD was associated with significantly lower local recurrence compared to EMR... ESD had a higher risk of perforation...
elements.reason: The abstract indicates the direction of effect and which group is favored for the compared outcomes.
The abstract does not contain a statement summarizing important limitations of the included evidence.

elements.quote: Conclusions ESD significantly reduces recurrence risk for colorectal LSTs > 20 mm compared with EMR but carries a higher perforation risk. Bleeding rates are comparable between the two techniques. ESD is recommended in expert centers where technical proficiency can mitigate perforation risk, while EMR-treated patients require closer surveillance due to higher recurrence.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of the results and their important implications.
The abstract does not specify the primary source of funding for the review.
The abstract does not provide the register name and registration number.

elements.quote: Colorectal laterally spreading tumors (LSTs) larger than 20 mm are significant precursors to colorectal cancer. Endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) and endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR) are widely used treatments, but their comparative efficacy and safety remain controversial.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly describes the current state of knowledge (LSTs are precursors, ESD/EMR are used) and important uncertainties (comparative efficacy and safety remain controversial).

elements.quote: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare ESD and EMR in terms of local recurrence, perforation, and delayed bleeding for colorectal LSTs > 20 mm.

elements.quote: Local recurrence (eight studies, n = 3024): Pooled recurrence rates: ESD 0.62% versus EMR 12.02%. OR 0.07 (95% CI 0.03-0.13; p < 0.01) with no heterogeneity ( I 2 = 0%, random-effects model) (Fig. 2). No publication bias was detected by funnel plot inspection or Egger's test ( p = 0.78) (Figs. 3 and 4). Delayed bleeding (eight studies, n = 3024): Pooled rates: ESD 3.65% versus EMR 3.75%. OR 1.01 (95% CI 0.65-1.55; p = 0.98) with no heterogeneity ( I 2 = 5%, randomeffects model) (Fig. 5). No publication bias was observed via funnel plot or Egger's test ( p = 0.42) (Figs. 6 and 7). Perforation (eight studies, n = 3024): Pooled rates: ESD 5.38% versus EMR 1.53%. OR 3.16 (95% CI 1.89-5.29; p < 0.01) with no heterogeneity ( I 2 = 0%, random-effects model) (Fig. 8). No publication bias was detected by funnel plot or Egger's test ( p = 0.45) (Figs. 9 and 10).

elements.quote: One of the key findings of this meta-analysis is the significant superiority of ESD in reducing recurrence rates of colorectal laterally spreading tumors (LSTs) larger than 20 mm. The overall recurrence rates in the ESD and EMR groups were 0.62% and 12.02%, respectively, which aligns closely with the results of studies such as that by Russo et al. [21].
elements.reason: The discussion section explicitly interprets the meta-analysis results by comparing them with findings from other specific studies (e.g., Russo et al., Terasaki et al., Saito et al.) and broader literature regarding safety and technique.

elements.quote: Most studies included in this meta-analysis were single-center or retrospective in nature. To minimize the risk of bias, we used the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale to assess the quality of nonrandomized studies. Furthermore, owing to missing original data, we were unable to compare the potential impact of different LST subtypes or lesion locations (e.g., proximal colon versus distal colon/rectum) on the efficacy and safety of the two techniques. Since different subtypes and locations may vary in biological behavior, technical difficulty, and prognosis (e.g., more advanced histology such as high-grade intraepithelial neoplasia or intramucosal carcinoma may increase the difficulty of en bloc resection), the absence of this information may affect the interpretation of the results.

elements.quote: Based on the current study and literature evidence [13, 23, 28], we recommend that patients who achieve curative en bloc ESD, given their extremely low recurrence risk, should undergo standard surveillance colonoscopy at 1 year postprocedure. In contrast, for cases managed with piecemeal ESD or any EMR, due to the significantly increased risk of residual lesion and recurrence, we strongly recommend shortening the surveillance interval to 6 months to enable early detection and intervention for residual or recurrent lesions.
